topicName: Architecture and Core Components (Runners, Jobs, Steps, Actions)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Architecture and Core Components of GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitHub Actions is a powerful continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform that allows you to automate your build, test, and deployment pipeline. To design efficient workflows, it is essential to understand its underlying architecture and core components: Runners, Jobs, Steps, and Actions."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Workflow Architecture Overview"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"At the highest level, a workflow is a configurable automated process defined in a YAML file located in the '.github/workflows' directory of your repository. Workflows are triggered by events such as a push, a pull request, or a scheduled time. Each workflow contains one or more jobs that can run sequentially or in parallel."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Runners"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"A runner is a server that runs your workflows when they are triggered. Each runner can run a single job at a time. GitHub provides hosted runners for Linux, Windows, and macOS, but you can also self-host your own runners if you require specific hardware, software, or network configurations."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"GitHub-Hosted Runners: Managed by GitHub, automatically provisioned, and wiped clean after every job execution."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Self-Hosted Runners: Hosted and managed by you, giving you full control over the environment and installed tools."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Jobs"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"A job is a set of steps in a workflow that executes on the same runner. By default, jobs run concurrently unless dependencies are defined using the 'needs' keyword. Because each job runs in a fresh instance of a runner environment, any data sharing between jobs must be explicitly handled, such as using artifacts."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Steps"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"A step is an individual task that can run commands in a job. Steps can run commands (actions), run setup scripts, or execute shell commands (like 'npm test'). Because steps run on the same runner, they share the workspace and state of that job."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Actions"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Actions are the building blocks of GitHub Actions. You can create your own actions, or use pre-built actions from the GitHub Marketplace. Actions perform complex and frequently repeated tasks, such as checking out your code, setting up a specific language runtime, or authenticating with cloud providers."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Putting It All Together: Example Workflow"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"The following YAML configuration demonstrates how Runners, Jobs, Steps, and Actions interact within a complete workflow."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"name: CI Pipeline
on: [push]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Run Tests
        run: npm test"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, 'runs-on: ubuntu-latest' specifies the Runner. The 'build' block represents the Job. The items under 'steps:' are the individual Steps, which leverage reusable Actions (like 'actions/checkout@v4') and shell commands (like 'npm test')."}]
